title: How Was the Bible Transmitted?
subtitle: Composition, copying, canon, and translation are different parts of the story
summary: The Bible preserves ancient texts through a long history of composition, copying, collection, and translation. Manuscripts show both substantial continuity and real variants, while churches differ over parts of the canon. These facts qualify claims of unchanged wording without proving that all biblical testimony is lost—or that Islam follows merely from a difficulty in Christian transmission.

seo.metaTitle: How Was the Bible Transmitted? An Honest History
seo.metaDescription: Composition, copying, canon, and translation explained through biblical evidence, with continuity, real variants, and the strongest Christian reply.

sections.title: Not a Lost Book, and Not a History Without Change
sections.body:
How can a reader trust a Bible copied across many centuries? The answer is neither that every word is unknowable nor that no change ever occurred. Surviving witnesses let scholars recover much wording with confidence and identify places where the evidence differs.

This matters to Muslims and Christians because the dispute concerns real claims about God and Jesus. An honest comparison starts with what each text and witness actually shows.

sections.title: Keep Four Questions Apart
sections.body:
Composition asks how a work was written and what sources it used. Copying asks how its wording traveled. Canon asks which works count as scripture. Translation asks how wording is represented in another language.

A dispute about a Gospel's author does not automatically show a later copy has different wording. A variant does not automatically remove a whole book from the canon. Confusing these questions creates a much more dramatic—but less accurate—story of 'corruption.'

sections.title: The Quran Affirms Earlier Revelation and Claims Authority
sections.body:
Quran 5:46–47 speaks positively of the Gospel's guidance, while 2:79 condemns writing and falsely claiming divine authority. Quran 5:48 describes the Quran as confirming earlier scripture and as a criterion over it.

Muslims therefore need not call every biblical sentence false to explain disagreement. But a Christian can fairly ask why the later Quran should judge earlier testimony. The answer must include a positive case for the Quran's authority; manuscript variation alone cannot supply it.

sections.title: The Bible Openly Describes Mediated Testimony
sections.body:
Luke 1:1–4 describes earlier accounts, received eyewitness testimony, and the author's investigation. This is a claim to careful historical narration, not a claim that Jesus dictated the Gospel word for word.

Christians commonly understand inspiration as God's work through such human authors. Muslims distinguish the Injil given to Jesus from later narratives about him. Those are different models of revelation. Luke's stated method is evidence for one model, not an admission of dishonesty.

sections.title: The Old Testament Record Shows Continuity and Diversity
sections.body:
The [Dead Sea Scrolls library](https://www.deadseascrolls.org.il/learn-about-the-scrolls/introduction?locale=en_US) describes biblical manuscripts that closely resemble the later Hebrew text alongside others with differences. This gives actual evidence of both careful preservation and textual plurality.

The New Testament likewise survives in many copied witnesses. [Codex Sinaiticus](https://codexsinaiticus.org/en/codex/default.aspx) preserves a complete New Testament in an early major codex. An original autograph need not survive for wording to be recoverable; the relationships and differences among copies are what textual critics examine.

sections.title: What Larger Variants Show
sections.body:
The longer ending of Mark and the woman accused of adultery are well-known examples where later readers encounter material absent from important early witnesses. Modern editions often flag them; the [Catholic note on John 7:53–8:11](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/john/8) explicitly discusses its later insertion.

That is meaningful evidence against an unqualified claim that no wording ever changed. It is not evidence that Christians invented every doctrine through hidden additions. Public textual notes are a strength of responsible scholarship, not something to ridicule.

sections.title: The Strongest Christian Reply Deserves an Answer
sections.body:
A Christian may say that many copies make variants visible and allow correction, and that central Christian beliefs do not depend on the disputed passages. Much of that reply is right: plentiful evidence can improve reconstruction, and no single famous variant erases the Christian case.

The remaining question is which source has authority when accounts conflict. Islam offers an early shared Quranic text and an explicit claim to correct earlier disputes. Its preservation supports access; its message and messenger must support divine authority. [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) gives that positive argument.

sections.title: Choose the Next Question Precisely
sections.body:
For wording, read [Textual Variants Explained](/articles/textual-variants-explained). For the Gospel authors and dates, read [Gospel Authorship and Dating](/articles/gospel-authorship-and-dating). For the table of contents, read [Biblical Canon Formation](/articles/biblical-canon-formation).

A fair conclusion about the Bible comes from those distinct inquiries—not a single slogan that it was perfectly unchanged or wholly lost.

sections.title: A Useful Check on a Dramatic Claim
sections.body: When someone says a verse was 'added,' ask which witnesses contain it, which omit it, and what a critical edition concludes. When someone says a book was 'chosen,' ask by whom, when, and for which community. Precise questions are more useful than an accusation made against the entire Bible at once.

sections.title: Read Christian Evidence in Christian Sources Too
sections.body: The primary manuscript and translation notes linked above let you inspect the issue directly. Metzger and Ehrman's textbook explains textual criticism; Bruce's canon study gives a serious Christian defense. Agreement with all their theology is not required to learn from their evidence.

quranVerses.arabic: وَقَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِعِيسَى ٱبْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًۭى وَنُورٌۭ وَمُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَهُدًۭى وَمَوْعِظَةًۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ ٱلْإِنجِيلِ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ ۚ وَمَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًۭا ۖ فَوَيْلٌۭ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌۭ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ
quranVerses.translation: So woe to those who write the "scripture" with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," in order to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ ۚ لِكُلٍّۢ جَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ شِرْعَةًۭ وَمِنْهَاجًۭا ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِى مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۖ فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ ۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًۭا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us, even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us, it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus; that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.
There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.
Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
For there are three who testify:

faq.question: Does copying over centuries make all biblical wording uncertain?
faq.answer: No. Many readings are well supported. Some remain disputed, and a smaller number involve substantial passages. Confidence should be stated passage by passage.

faq.question: Does an original autograph have to survive?
faq.answer: No. Copies can preserve early wording, and comparison can recover it with varying confidence. An autograph's absence is a limitation, not proof of total loss.

faq.question: Do Muslims believe every biblical sentence is false?
faq.answer: No. Islam affirms earlier revelation and recognizes truth in the surviving Bible, while treating the Quran as final authority. That authority requires its own positive case.

faq.question: Is translation itself corruption?
faq.answer: No. Translation is an interpretation of wording in another language and can be careful or mistaken. It should not be confused with a manuscript addition or change in canon.

faq.question: Did Nicaea select all the Bible's books?
faq.answer: No. That familiar claim misrepresents a longer history of use, debate, and recognition. The canon article examines actual early lists.
